Request.name: Request
Request.comment: Represents a request that includes categorization for both request and assignment with ITIL compliance tracking

RequestAssignment.name: RequestAssignment
RequestAssignment.comment: Represents an assignment of a request to users or areas.

AssignedUser.name: AssignedUser
AssignedUser.comment: Represents the users assigned to a request, including the coordinator.

RequestPriorityType.name: RequestPriorityType
RequestPriorityType.comment: Represents a catalog of possible priority levels for requests or assignments.

RequirementComplianceTracking.name: RequirementComplianceTracking
RequirementComplianceTracking.comment: Tracks compliance with requirements for a specific request.

CustomerSatisfactionSurvey.name: CustomerSatisfactionSurvey
CustomerSatisfactionSurvey.comment: Tracks customer satisfaction surveys for closed requests.

RequestChangeLog.name: RequestChangeLog
RequestChangeLog.comment: Logs changes to requests for auditing purposes.

RequestDataroom.name: RequestDataroom
RequestDataroom.comment: Junction table for Request-Dataroom relationship (one-to-one enforced by unique constraints)

Area.name: Area
Area.comment:
Represents an organizational area within a tenant.
Areas allow grouping of users, categories, and request assignments in a specific organizational scope.

UserTenantArea.name: UserTenantArea
UserTenantArea.comment:
Represents the assignment of users to areas with specific roles.
This model acts as an intermediate table for associating users, areas, and area-specific roles.

AreaRole.name: AreaRole
AreaRole.comment:
Represents roles that are specific to an area.
Area roles define features and responsibilities of users within a specific organizational area.

AreaRoleFeature.name: AreaRoleFeature
AreaRoleFeature.comment:
Links area-specific roles to features.
This model defines which features are granted to roles within a specific area.

RequestHierarchyLevel.name: RequestHierarchyLevel
RequestHierarchyLevel.comment: Represents a level within a request hierarchy.

RequestCategory.name: RequestCategory
RequestCategory.comment:
Represents a request category, with SLA and required documents.
Business Rule: A category should only be activated (isActive = true) if it has a complete chain of children
down to the last hierarchy level. This ensures users can complete request forms without encountering
"No options" errors. Validation is enforced at the application level.
Business Rule: Only leaf categories (categories without subcategories) can be selected directly in requests.
Parent/intermediate categories are used for navigation and organization but cannot be the final selection.

GuideDocument.name: GuideDocument
GuideDocument.comment: Represents a guide document used to resolve a request.

Requirement.name: Requirement
Requirement.comment: Represents a specific requirement for a request/assignment category.

RequestCategoryRequirement.name: RequestCategoryRequirement
RequestCategoryRequirement.comment: Links a requirement to a specific category.

RequirementType.name: RequirementType
RequirementType.comment: Represents a type of a requirement.

AssignmentHierarchyLevel.name: AssignmentHierarchyLevel
AssignmentHierarchyLevel.comment: Represents a level within an assignment hierarchy.

AssignmentCategory.name: AssignmentCategory
AssignmentCategory.comment:
Represents an assignment category, linked to specific rules and an area.
Business Rule: Only leaf categories (categories without subcategories) can be selected directly in requests.
Parent/intermediate categories are used for navigation and organization but cannot be the final selection.

ExecutionFlowDefinition.name: ExecutionFlowDefinition
ExecutionFlowDefinition.comment:
# Workflow Execution System

## Core Workflow Definitions
@namespace CoreWorkflow
@erd CoreWorkflow
Represents a versioned workflow template containing nodes and edges

Relationships:
╠═► nodes: Contains all component nodes
╠═► edges: Defines transitions between nodes
╠═► executions: Runtime instances using this template
╚═► requestCategory: Business process classification

ExecutionNodeDefinition.name: ExecutionNodeDefinition
ExecutionNodeDefinition.comment:
Atomic unit in workflow execution path
@minItems 1

ExecutionEdgeDefinition.name: ExecutionEdgeDefinition
ExecutionEdgeDefinition.comment:
Defines transitions between nodes with conditional logic
@minItems 1

ExecutionNodeGuide.name: ExecutionNodeGuide

ExecutionModelInstance.name: ExecutionModelInstance

ExecutionModelHistory.name: ExecutionModelHistory

Role.name: Role
Role.comment:
Represents a system role within a tenant.
Roles define sets of features that can be assigned to users.

Module.name: Module
Module.comment:
Module also known as a feature or section of the application that can be enabled or disabled
in other terms, it also works as feature flags for the application to enable or disable features
based on if the module is enabled or disabled for the tenant or user

NOTE: Module is now GLOBAL (not tenant-scoped). Use TenantModule to enable/disable modules per tenant.

Feature.name: Feature
Feature.comment:
Represents features in the system. 
A single table handles both global features and area-specific features using the `scope` field.
Features are linked to modules for better organization and can be assigned to global roles or area roles.

NOTE: Feature is now GLOBAL (not tenant-scoped). Availability is controlled via:
- PlanFeature: Defines which features are available in a plan (with limits)
- TenantModule: Allows tenants to disable entire modules

TenantModule.name: TenantModule
TenantModule.comment:
Links tenants to modules, allowing tenants to enable/disable modules independently of their plan.
This provides flexibility for tenants to disable modules they don't need, even if their plan includes them.

If no TenantModule record exists for a tenant-module pair, the module is considered ENABLED by default.
